Experimental feature testing in progress, please pay attention to the comments

Some concerns, see inline comments. The main one is that the completion check in lod_ost_alloc_rr() is much weaker than the equivalent one in lod_ost_alloc_qos(), so the RR path can return success for a parity component that has fewer objects than it has raid sets. There is also a non-EC behaviour change in the qos allocator that looks like it slipped in with the EC work and may deserve its own patch.

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The main ones are in the round-robin allocator, where the EC fallbacks can hand back a layout with two stripes of the same raid set on one OST, and the QoS acceptance threshold change, which is not limited to EC components.

sanity-ec.sh still has no case that allocates a wide component with `-c -1` together with `--ec`; every test computes an explicit stripe count that leaves room for the parities, which is not how layouts are specified in production. That point was raised earlier in this review and still looks uncovered.

Uploaded patch set 49.

Patch Set 53:

(7 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. The raid-set rules look complete on the round-robin side but not on the QoS side, and the new tests only exercise round-robin: lod_ost_alloc_qos() is skipped whenever free space is balanced (ltd_qos_is_usable()), which is the steady state of a fresh test filesystem, so 27d/27e/27f never validate the QoS placement path. Would it be worth driving those cases through QoS too, e.g. by setting lod.*.qos_threshold_rr=0 and unbalancing the OSTs, so the raid-set invariants are checked on both allocators?

Patch Set 54:

(3 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Patchset 54 looks like it was uploaded from a stale local commit. Both revisions sit on the same parent, and every difference between patchset 53 and patchset 54 in lod_qos.c moves the code backwards to an earlier version of the same hunk.

What patchset 54 gives up relative to patchset 53:

- the llc_dstripe_count guard on the round-robin ec_split_stripes() resplit
- `else if (stripe_idx)` around the llc_stripe_count store, so a pass that placed nothing writes 0 again
- the `rc >= 0` guard before `rc = -ENOSPC`, so -EINPROGRESS is overwritten again
- setting `overstriped` after lod_ec_add_data(), and clearing LOV_PATTERN_OVERSTRIPING after the EC fallbacks instead of before them

commit.subject: LU-19852 lod: raidset aware stripe allocator
commit.message:
LU-19852 lod: raidset aware stripe allocator

Make the qos and rr stripe allocators raidset aware.

For data allocations:
- -c: prefer unique OSTs for all data stripes (multi-raidset mins may
  be relaxed; geometry can shrink when OSTs are short)
- -C: require unique OSTs within each raidset; OSTs may be reused
  across raidsets via overstriping

For EC data components without overstriping (-c), both lod_ost_alloc_qos()
and lod_ost_alloc_rr() may reduce the requested data stripe count when at
least 75% of the request can still be placed, then resplit the geometry.
Parity and overstriped (-C) components are not rescaled this way.

For parity allocations:
Parities can reuse OSTs selected for data stripes as long as they are
reused in a different raidset.
